posts.title: Cheap to Build: where the cost of building software actually went
posts.description: Building software has gotten dramatically cheaper over the last three years thanks to generative AI, and is continuing to improve with newer models. But did better software come out the other end? Here's where I think the cost actually went, and why the next model release won't be the thing that fixes it.

posts.title: Is this sustainable?
posts.description: I've been a principal engineer at the same company for three years now. The job I do today and the job I started in 2023 share a title and a level, and not much else. AI has reshaped both what I do and how I do it, and I've been meaning to write down what that actually looks like from inside the role rather than the version you read about in productivity reports.

posts.title: Journal v1.0: A Simple Go Project That Grew Up
posts.description: I've been working on a little side project called Journal for several years - a simple web-based journalling application written in Go. After a long time in pre-release, I recently shipped v1.0, and wanted to write about what it is, what changed, and why I still think it's worth maintaining and growing.
